sections.label: Green Mark scheme introduction
sections.summary: Singapore's effort to green the built environment began about two decades ago in 2005 with the Green Mark scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Our journey to green our built environment began about two decades ago in 2005, with the introduction of the Green Mark scheme.

sections.label: SGBMP co-development and targets
sections.summary: The SGBMP was co-developed with over 5,000 individuals and sets out three targets, or 80-80-80 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As reflected in its title "Building our Green Future Together", this edition of the SGBMP was co-developed with over 5,000 individuals across the built environment value chain as well as the wider community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: It sets out three ambitious targets, or "80-80-80 in 2030".

sections.label: Mandatory Energy Improvement regime
sections.summary: The Bill introduces the Mandatory Energy Improvement regime, planned for the third quarter of 2025, to tackle emissions from energy-intensive buildings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To tackle the emissions arising from this group of existing energy-intensive buildings, this Bill will introduce the Mandatory Energy Improvement, or MEI regime planned for the third quarter of 2025.

sections.label: MEI regime building coverage
sections.summary: The MEI regime will apply to commercial, healthcare, institutional, and sports and recreation buildings with a GFA of 5,000 sqm and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For a start, the MEI regime will apply to commercial buildings, healthcare institutions, institutional buildings, as well as sports and recreation buildings that have a GFA of 5,000 square metres (sqm) and above.

sections.label: MEI audit and EEIP process
sections.summary: After an MEI audit notice, a specified individual must be appointed within 90 days, with audit report and EEIP submitted to BCA within one year and measures implemented within three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Upon being issued an MEI audit notice, the building owner is to appoint a specified individual within 90 days to carry out an energy audit of the building's major energy consuming systems, such as the building’s chiller and hot water systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: With the findings of the energy audit, the specified individual is to develop an Energy Efficiency Improvement Plan, or EEIP with proposed measures to reduce the building's EUI by 10% from pre-audit levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The building owner is then required to submit the audit report, which includes the EEIP, to BCA within one year from the issuance of the MEI audit notice and implement the measures in the EEIP within three years from the submission of the audit report.

sections.label: Retrofitting savings and carbon tax
sections.summary: Retrofitting works cut energy consumption by around 40%, have an average payback period of around six years, and Singapore's carbon tax will rise from $25 to $45 in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The retrofitting works included the upgrading of the existing chiller plant to a more efficient one, the redesign of the air-distribution system to better cater to the building's cooling demand, as well as the implementation of an energy management system with intelligent controls to more effectively monitor the performance of building systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: These measures have resulted in a significant reduction of the building's energy consumption by around 40%, which translates to a reduction in its annual electricity bills by the same extent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Beyond this case example, extensive retrofitting works, such as those implemented by the Thong Chai Building, generally have an average payback period of around six years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This means that building owners should be able to offset the upfront cost of the retrofit through downstream cost savings within an average of six years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: After this six-year period, owners will still continue to reap further savings over the rest of the building's lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This House would also be aware that Singapore's carbon tax will be further raised from $25 per tonne of emissions today to $45 in 2026, with a view to reaching between $50 and $80 by 2030.

sections.label: Co-funding for energy efficiency retrofits
sections.summary: Building owners can receive up to 50% co-funding support for energy efficiency retrofits, with caps depending on Green Mark certification level achieved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under this incentive scheme, building owners can receive up to 50% co-funding support to implement energy efficiency retrofits at various caps, depending on the level of Green Mark certification standard achieved.

sections.label: Statutory duties for facade inspections
sections.summary: The regulations set out statutory duties for FIs on due diligence, supervision of engaged persons or inspection companies, and immediate notification of unsafe facades.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The regulations will set out the statutory duties for FIs to: (a) exercise due diligence in carrying facade inspections in accordance with the CP's instructions and directions; (b) personally supervise in full-time any other person or inspection company engaged by the CP to conduct the inspection; and (c) notify the CP immediately of any unsafe facade.

sections.label: Drop in building energy use intensity
sections.summary: BCA reports that overall energy use intensity of buildings dropped by 29% between 2008 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: BCA reports that the overall energy use intensity of our buildings has dropped by 29% between 2008 and 2023.

sections.label: Appointment for energy audits
sections.summary: Section 22FB provides that a mechanical engineer, an energy auditor or any prescribed class of individuals may be appointed to carry out an energy audit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 22FB provides that a mechanical engineer, an energy auditor or any prescribed class of individuals may be appointed to carry out an energy audit.

sections.label: Previous Green Mark Incentive Schemes
sections.summary: The Government previously had Green Mark Incentive Schemes to help improve the environmental standards of buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government previously had Green Mark Incentive Schemes to help improve the environmental standards of buildings.

sections.label: Green Economy Regulatory Initiative launch
sections.summary: In 2022, MTI launched the Green Economy Regulatory Initiative to consolidate sandbox efforts by Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2022, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) launched the Green Economy Regulatory Initiative (GERI) to consolidate sandbox efforts by Government agencies.

sections.label: Financial support for building owners
sections.summary: Asks if Government can expand the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green, Energy Efficiency Grant and Green Mark Incentive Scheme to ease compliance costs for building owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address the financial burden that many building owners, particularly smaller enterprises, may face in complying with the requirements of this Bill, can the Government consider leveraging and expanding the Enterprise Financing Scheme – Green, the Energy Efficiency Grant and the Green Mark Incentive Scheme?

sections.label: Expanding Energy Efficiency Grant
sections.summary: Asks about plans to expand the Energy Efficiency Grant to construction, process, maritime, data centres and other energy-consuming sectors by year end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, I would like to ask about the Government's plans to expand the Energy Efficiency Grant to include construction, process, maritime and data centres and their users by the end of this year as well as other sectors which are also energy consumers.

sections.label: Training sustainability professionals and auditors
sections.summary: Cites US energy auditor shortage delays and recommends Government work with institutes, industry bodies and agencies to increase training and certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under the Energy Independence and Security Act in the United States, a shortage of energy auditors led to significant delays in compliance, creating a backlog that undermined the overall efficiency of the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I recommend that the Government work with institutes of higher learning, industry bodies and agencies to increase the training and certification of both sustainability professionals and energy auditors.

sections.label: EV charging in building EUI
sections.summary: Asks how EV charging stations, particularly in malls and office car parks, will be factored into a building's EUI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, with the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), how will EV charging stations, particularly in malls and office car parks, will be factored into a building's EUI.

sections.label: Flexibility for heritage buildings
sections.summary: Asks if Government can consider flexibility clauses letting owners of heritage buildings apply for extensions or exemptions where retrofitting would compromise integrity or technology is not feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Particularly, for heritage or historically significant buildings, can the Government consider flexibility clauses, allowing building owners to apply for extensions or exemptions where retrofitting would compromise the building's integrity or where the technology for upgrades is not yet feasible.

sections.label: Early compliance incentives and coordination
sections.summary: Proposes incentive programmes for early compliance and says strong inter-agency coordination is essential to avoid overly conservative risk assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This spurred innovation and created a competitive environment for energy efficiency solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose the introduction of incentive programmes for building owners who comply early with the Bill's requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As part of the Bill's implementation, strong inter-agency coordination will be essential to ensure that no single agency, such as those involved in perhaps rooftop solar installations or future green technologies, applies overly conservative risk assessments.

sections.label: Streamlining green retrofit processes
sections.summary: The feedback leads to a recommendation to streamline processes and align agencies for green retrofits and future green systems like battery energy storage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on this feedback, we recommend streamlining processes and ensuring alignment across agencies to support not only green retrofits but also the future deployment of green systems, like battery energy storage systems.

sections.label: Building emissions and greening progress
sections.summary: Buildings account for about 20% of Singapore's carbon emissions and over a third of electricity use, with 58% greened by GFA as of December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Presently, buildings account for around 20% of Singapore carbon emissions and more than a third of Singapore's electricity consumption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of December 2023, current efforts have greened about 58% of our buildings by GFA.

sections.label: Scheme disbursement and MEI threshold
sections.summary: The passage asks how much was disbursed under a 2022 scheme, its impact, expected take-up under the MEI regime, and the threshold's ambition and review frequency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How much has been disbursed under this scheme and to what impact since it was first introduced in 2022 and does the Government foresee an increased take-up with the introduction of the MEI regime?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How ambitious will this pre-determined threshold be and how often will it be reviewed to ensure that we are keeping with our national targets?

sections.label: MEI rollout timeline and communication
sections.summary: The passage asks for the Ministry's projected timeline for MEI introduction and rollout to older buildings and how processes and timelines will be communicated to owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the BCA's preliminary estimation looks at not that many buildings involved in the introduction of the MEI regime and I note that these building owners will receive an advanced audit notice, I would like to ask what is the Ministry projected timeline for the introduction and progressive rollout of MEI for all older buildings?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As a whole, how would these processes and timelines be communicated to building owners?

sections.label: Greening 80% of buildings by 2030
sections.summary: With the MEI regime, the speaker hopes to close gaps and fulfil the commitment to green 80% of buildings by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the introduction of the MEI regime, I hope that we can close the gaps steadily and fulfil our commitment to green 80% of our buildings by 2030.

sections.label: Basis for approving MEI amendments
sections.summary: The passage asks on what basis approval would be given to a building owner seeking to amend the specified energy use intensity reduction or energy efficiency improvement plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The new sections 22FM and 22FN of the Bill would empower the CBC to require owners of identified energy-intensive buildings to appoint a specified individual to carry out an audit on the energy use of the building as well as provide the building owner with an energy efficiency improvement plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, under the new section 22FO, the same building owner can apply to reduce the energy use intensity of the building by a lower percentage than the approved reduction and/or amend the proposed energy efficiency improvement plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On what basis would approval be given to a building owner seeking to amend the specified reduction in energy use intensity and/or the proposed energy efficiency improvement plan?

sections.label: Prescribed maintenance period question
sections.summary: Asks how long the prescribed maintenance period is and whether one common period applies to all buildings under the updated regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How long is the prescribed maintenance period and does a common prescribed maintenance period apply to all buildings under the updated regime?

sections.label: MEI regime energy reduction
sections.summary: The top quarter of building typologies in energy consumption will be placed on MEI and must cut energy use intensity by 10% and maintain it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Tangible initiatives like the MEI regime are steps in the right direction to shift us from merely talking about it to doing something about it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the top quarter of all building typologies in energy consumption will be placed on MEI.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They will be required to reduce their energy use intensity by 10% and maintain it, which is a very specific goal.

sections.label: Air-conditioning share of emissions
sections.summary: Household and building air-conditioning use is 19% of Singapore's carbon emissions, second after the industrial sector's 60%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Household and building use of air-conditioning alone constitutes 19% of Singapore’s carbon emissions, making it the second highest source of emissions in Singapore after the industrial sector, which accounts for 60%.

sections.label: Hybrid and naturally ventilated buildings
sections.summary: To be resilient in a worst-case energy scenario, buildings should convert to hybrid natural ventilation and new buildings should default to natural ventilation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure we are resilient in a worst-case scenario where energy supply may decline to the point where it will have to be reserved for essential services, or become too expensive for Singapore to procure, we need to do two things: one, reverse this process and convert over the next few decades buildings that are currently fully air-conditioned to hybrid buildings with more natural ventilation; and two, make natural ventilation the default norm for new buildings, starting from now into the future.

sections.label: Mandating ventilation and strata acquisition
sections.summary: The speaker hopes natural ventilation is mandated in phases for commercial buildings and suggests a legal mechanism to acquire strata units, with grants over about 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Whilst increasing natural ventilation is now an intentional component of HDB’s design process for public housing and spaces, I hope this can be mandated in progressive phases for commercial buildings as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Similar to the Land Acquisition Act which enabled the Government to acquire land for the construction of public infrastructure, the Government may want to consider a similar legal mechanism for strata units to be acquired, or supported, where necessary, so that parts of a fully air-conditioned building can be opened up to achieve natural light and ventilation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This can be done step by step with helpful doses of grants and support from the Government over the next 20 years or so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One of the things that COVID-19 has shown us is that open ventilation spaces also help to reduce risks of transmission in the event of virus outbreaks.

sections.label: EUI threshold and five-year period
sections.summary: The EUI threshold is pegged at the 75th percentile for each building sub-typology, prescribed in subsidiary legislation, and fixed for five years from 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The EUI threshold is pegged at the 75th percentile of the EUI range for each building sub-typology and will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The EUI threshold will be fixed for a period of five years from 2025.

sections.label: MEI regime building typologies
sections.summary: The MEI regime applies only to four broad building typologies: commercial, healthcare, institutional, and sports and recreation buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To clarify, the MEI regime applies only to four broad building typologies, namely, commercial buildings, healthcare facilities, institutional buildings and sports and recreation buildings.

sections.label: First MEI audit notices
sections.summary: The first batch of MEI audit notices will be issued in the third quarter of 2025, with fewer than 100 energy-intensive buildings expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In my opening speech, I shared that we intend to issue the first batch of MEI audit notices in the third quarter of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We expect that there will be fewer than 100 energy-intensive buildings in this first batch.

sections.label: Green leases data collection
sections.summary: BCA does not collect data on the uptake of green leases in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To Ms Nadia's query about the uptake of green leases in the past year, BCA does not collect such data.

sections.label: Maintaining improved EUI reduction
sections.summary: Building owners must maintain the improved EUI reduction for a year after completing energy efficiency improvement measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As mentioned earlier, building owners are to maintain the improved EUI reduction for a year after the completion of the energy efficiency improvement measures.

sections.label: Annual energy performance data submission
sections.summary: Building owners will be required to submit their building's energy performance data annually to fulfil MEI regime requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To Ms Nadia and Ms See's query about efforts that BCA will take to ensure that building owners remain on track to fulfil the requirements of the MEI regime, building owners will be required to submit their building's energy performance data annually.

sections.label: Percentage versus absolute EUI reduction
sections.summary: A percentage reduction was chosen instead of an absolute EUI reduction figure because building EUI can differ significantly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Ms Nadia also asked if there may be plans to prescribe an absolute EUI reduction figure instead of the 10% reduction in the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have gone with a percentage reduction as the EUI of buildings can differ quite significantly, even if they are of the same building typology and in the 75th percentile.

sections.label: Building owner funding support
sections.summary: Since 2022, 11 applications were approved with about $1.3 million committed, and a mid-term review is underway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2022, we have approved 11 applications and committed about $1.3 million in funding support to building owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We expect the utilisation to increase with the implementation of the MEI regime.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We are also undertaking a mid-term review of the scheme to consider ways to enhance support to building owners.

sections.label: EEG application via Business Grants Portal
sections.summary: Interested construction firms may apply for EEG on the Business Grants Portal from the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Interested construction firms may apply for EEG on the Business Grants Portal from the end of this year.

sections.label: GBIC 2.0 South Beach Tower project
sections.summary: GBIC 2.0 supports building energy efficiency research, and South Beach Tower Office will receive up to $1.6 million for air-conditioning solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: One such programme is the Green Buildings Innovation Cluster 2.0 (GBIC 2.0), a programme which supports the research, development and demonstration of building energy efficiency technologies and innovations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Just last week, at the International Built Environment Week, we announced an exciting demonstration project by South Beach Tower Office under GBIC 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: They will be receiving up to $1.6 million of funding support to implement novel solutions to enhance the energy efficiency of the tower's air-conditioning systems, with the goal of achieving 75% energy efficiency improvement from 2005 levels.

sections.label: GMIS-EB 2.0 co-funding support
sections.summary: GMIS-EB 2.0 provides co-funding support to existing building owners who wish to redesign air-conditioned spaces into naturally ventilated spaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: GMIS-EB 2.0 also provides co-funding support to existing building owners who wish to redesign existing air-conditioned spaces to naturally ventilated spaces.
